en.subject: The Excel problem at {{company}}
en.body_html:
Hi {{first_name}},

Following up on my last note. One thing we hear from every manufacturer we talk to: planners are still building the entire weekly plan in Excel, running what-if scenarios by hand, and communicating changes through email and chat. Even companies with SAP.

The real cost goes well beyond the planner hours. It is the material shortages discovered at line startup instead of during planning, the overproduction that gets sold at a discount, and the 3+ hours a day spent in alignment meetings because there's no shared plan of record.

Acme replaces that manual cycle. Our agents generate optimized daily sequences that respect line capacity, check material availability before scheduling, and push changes to production in real time. No more missed emails, no more surprises on the floor.

Would love to show you how this works for a facility like yours. 15 min is all I need.

Alex

es.subject: El problema del Excel en {{company}}
es.body_html:

El costo real va mucho más allá de las horas del planificador. Son los faltantes de material que se descubren al arrancar la línea en lugar de durante la planificación, la sobreproducción que se vende con descuento, y las 3+ horas al día en juntas de alineación porque no hay un plan compartido de referencia.

Acme reemplaza ese ciclo manual. Nuestros agentes generan secuencias diarias optimizadas que respetan la capacidad de línea, verifican disponibilidad de materiales antes de programar, y comunican cambios a producción en tiempo real. Sin correos perdidos, sin sorpresas en piso.

Me encantaría mostrarte cómo funciona para una planta como la suya. Solo necesito 15 min.

Alex

en.subject: The Excel file that runs production at {{company}}
en.body_html:
Hi {{first_name}},

We keep seeing the same pattern at giant manufacturing operations: the weekly production plan lives in one Excel file, owned by one planner. When that planner is in a meeting (and the planners we've talked to spend 3+ hours a day in alignment meetings), the floor stops asking and starts guessing. That gap shows up as OTIF penalties (retailers charge ~3% of non-compliant shipment volume) and waste that nobody traces back.

We built Acme (acme.example.com) to replace the Excel-and-meetings cycle: agents that plan, check material availability, and push changes to production in real time.

If you want the 60-second walkthrough I'm sending to plant directors, reply "send it" and I'll send it back. If it's not the right time at {{company}}, no problem at all.

Alex
